question.prompt: Consider all polynomials of a complex variable, \(P(z) = 4z^4 + az^3\) \(+ bz^2 + cz + d,\) where \(a,\) \(b,\) \(c,\) and \(d\) are integers, \(0 \le d \le c \le b \le a \le 4,\) and the polynomial has a zero \(z_0\) with \(|z_0| = 1.\) What is the sum of all values \(P(1)\) over all the polynomials with these properties?

solutions.explanation:
The ordered coefficients suggest looking at their successive differences, because those differences are nonnegative. Define
\[
(u_1,u_2,u_3,u_4,u_5)
=(4-a,a-b,b-c,c-d,d).
\]
These are nonnegative integers with sum \(4\). Conversely, every such vector uniquely recovers allowed coefficients by summing from the right, for example \(d=u_5\), \(c=u_4+u_5\), and so on.

Let \(z\) be a zero with \(|z|=1\). Since \(P(1)\ge4\), we have \(z\ne1\); also \(z\ne0\). Multiplying by \(1-z\) makes the successive differences appear:
\[
(1-z)P(z)=-4z^5+\sum_{j=1}^{5}u_jz^{5-j}.
\]
At the zero, division by \(z^5\) gives
\[
4=\sum_{j=1}^{5}u_jz^{-j}.
\]

Every \(z^{-j}\) has modulus \(1\), so its real part is at most \(1\), with equality only when \(z^{-j}=1\). Taking real parts and using \(\sum u_j=4\), we obtain
\[
0=\sum_{j=1}^{5}u_j\bigl(1-\operatorname{Re}(z^{-j})\bigr).
\]
Every summand is nonnegative. Consequently,
\[
u_j>0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad z^j=1.
\]

At least one \(u_j\) is positive, so \(z\) is a root of unity. Let \(k\) be the least positive integer with \(z^k=1\). Then \(2\le k\le5\). Moreover, \(k\) divides every index \(j\) for which \(u_j>0\): writing \(j=qk+r\), with \(0\le r<k\), would otherwise give \(z^r=1\) with a smaller positive exponent.

There are therefore only these possibilities:

If \(k=2\), positive differences can occur only at indices \(2,4\). Thus \(u_2=t\), \(u_4=4-t\), and the others are zero, where \(t=0,1,2,3,4\).

If \(k=3\), only \(u_3\) can be positive, giving \(u_3=4\).

If \(k=4\), only \(u_4\) can be positive. This vector is already included in the first family, so it contributes no new polynomial.

If \(k=5\), only \(u_5\) can be positive, giving \(u_5=4\).

All these vectors do work. Choose \(z=-1\) for the first family, a nontrivial cube root of unity for the second, and a nontrivial fifth root of unity for the third. In each case all positive \(u_j\) have \(z^j=1\), so the displayed identity gives \((1-z)P(z)=0\). Because \(z\ne1\), this proves \(P(z)=0\). The three families of difference vectors are disjoint, so they give exactly seven distinct polynomials.

To evaluate their contributions, notice that \(u_j\) occurs in exactly \(j\) of the five coefficients \(4,a,b,c,d\). Hence
\[
P(1)=u_1+2u_2+3u_3+4u_4+5u_5.
\]
The first family gives \(16-2t\), namely \(16,14,12,10,8\), whose sum is \(60\). The other two polynomials give \(12\) and \(20\). Both occurrences of \(12\) are included because they come from different polynomials. The requested sum is
\[
60+12+20=\boxed{92},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
